reviewer: builder (the agent session that wrote the generator)
findings: The plan reads as a half-ellipse crescent of twenty houses, as the street view and the oblique show.
Three storeys: a plain ground storey, then two storeys behind a giant Ionic order with one sash to a bay on each.
Proportions were set from pixel measurements on the street view: ground storey 4.4 m against 7.2 m columns, slender columns about eleven diameters tall.
Each capital reads as Ionic, with two scrolls side by side under the abacus; each column stands on a plinth block on the band.
Entablature, modillion cornice and balustrade run unbroken round all four sides and mitre cleanly at the four corners.
Every sash sits in a reveal with a frame, glazing bars and glass, with floors and walls behind; every door has panels, a fanlight and a threshold.
The roof is closed: slate ranges, lead gutters and flat, party upstands, stacks with pots and dormers; both ends are hipped.
The convex side and both ends are complete elevations. Nothing floats and nothing sits below grade.
open_notes: The roof plan reference shows a different, shorter building; it informs roof character only.
The comparison cameras are approximate; in the street view the near end renders larger than the reference.
Sunken areas, their steps and the bridges to the doors are left out; railings stand at grade.
The reference stacks are broader and stand closer to the front than the model's.
Bays on the convex side widen toward the ends, from 2.7 m to 3.7 m.
Thin railing bars and glazing bars break up in distant views; a renderer sampling effect.
At 176,290 triangles the model is just under the usual 180,000 ceiling.
Each corner room at the two ends has windows in two walls, so a diagonal line of sight passes through glass alone there.
changes_since_v002: Two faults found by the builder's own geometric audit are fixed. The spine wall of each end house ran out to the outside face of the end, showing as a thin blade up the middle end column; it now stops at the inner face of the wall. Floors were one slab to a house and stopped up to 0.32 m short of the convex wall; they are now laid bay by bay and meet both walls. The door leaf is a shade darker than its panels so the six panels read. The oblique comparison camera was moved nearer the reference viewpoint.

geometric_audit.method: rays cast in through every sash at seven headings and three pitches, 7,434 in all, on the v002 geometry
geometric_audit.result: four rays pass through glass only: each enters a first-floor sash on the convex side beside a corner and leaves through a sash in the end. These are corner rooms with windows in two walls, as built.

changes_since_v003: Five small faults found by reading the model against its own numbers are fixed. Each window sill shared a plane with the top of the wall beneath it and now stands 12 mm proud. The iron guards stopped 20 mm short of the column plinths and 60 mm above the band; the bottom rail is now let into the plinths and an end post stands on the band at each end. The railing returns beside each door path stood 20 mm above the paving and now stand on it. The cushion of each capital started 20 mm above the necking, leaving a slit, and now sits on it. The band the columns stand on ran 80 mm under the first floor at the same level and now stops at the wall. Faces buried in a neighbour (the backs and tops of modillions, the ends of pedestals and plinths) are left off, which saves 3,400 triangles.
